faq.q: What does a convex lens do?
faq.a: A convex lens is thicker in the middle. It bends light rays inwards so they meet at a focal point. It is also called a converging lens.

faq.q: What does a concave lens do?
faq.a: A concave lens is thinner in the middle. It spreads light rays apart, as if they came from a point behind the lens. It is also called a diverging lens.
The focal point is where parallel rays meet after passing through a convex lens. Its distance from the lens is the focal length.

faq.q: Which lens is used for short sight?
faq.a: A concave lens. It spreads the light slightly so the eye focuses it on the retina instead of in front of it.

faq.q: Why does a magnifying glass make things bigger?
faq.a: It is a convex lens. When an object is closer than the focal point, the lens makes a large, upright, virtual image.
asks: How does a magnifying glass work?

facts: A convex (converging) lens brings parallel rays to a real focal point.
Short sight is corrected with concave lenses; long sight with convex lenses.
